title: Shift-dragging a marquee adds what it sweeps to the selection
goal: Sweeping a rubber band always starts the selection over. Holding shift while you sweep should add everything the band takes in to what you already picked, so you can build a selection out of two or three sweeps instead of getting it right in one.
notes: Half of the original task shipped on 2026-09-03 (commit 3d46af2): a shift-click that lands on bare canvas now spares the selection, through BareCanvasPress in PhotonzCore, latched at mouse-down in CanvasView. What is left is the DRAG: CanvasView still starts a MarqueeDrag that replaces the selection whether or not shift is down. Note the collision the earlier task left alone: shift over an empty press currently also means constrain-the-band-to-a-square (read in CanvasView.mouseUp), so the square constraint needs a new modifier or has to go. BareCanvasPress is the place to put the new rule so it is tested first.
acceptance: Shift-dragging a band on the canvas adds every layer it fully contains to the existing selection
A plain sweep still replaces the selection the way it does today
The outlines after a shift-sweep show every picked layer, swept and clicked
One undo is not involved: this changes what is picked, not the picture

log.note: triage 2026-09-03: half of this shipped in 3d46af2 (a shift-click that misses keeps the selection). Narrowed to the shift-SWEEP, which still replaces.
